about.title: About Credit Card Payoff Calculator - Debt Elimination Tool
about.description: The Credit Card Payoff Calculator helps you compare payoff timelines, payment plans, and interest totals for credit card balances. It shows estimated payoff duration and total interest under different payment strategies so you can review tradeoffs between minimum payments and faster repayment. Use it as a planning reference when organizing debt-repayment scenarios.

faq.q: Should I pay more than the minimum on my credit cards?
faq.a: Paying more than the minimum generally shortens the repayment timeline and reduces total interest, though the effect depends on your balance, APR, and payment amount. Use the calculator to compare scenarios before making a plan.

faq.q: Which credit card should I pay off first?
faq.a: The debt avalanche method suggests paying minimums on all cards while putting extra money toward the highest interest rate card. The debt snowball method focuses on the smallest balance first for psychological motivation.

faq.q: How much should I pay toward credit card debt each month?
faq.a: The amount depends on your balance, APR, minimum payment rules, and budget. Higher payments generally reduce total interest and shorten the payoff timeline, but use the calculator to compare scenarios based on your own inputs.

faq.q: Is it worth transferring balances to a 0% APR card?
faq.a: Balance transfers may be useful in some cases, especially when the promotional APR, transfer fee, and repayment timeline fit your situation. Compare fees, timing, and the post-promotion APR before deciding.
